data.narrative:
Nucleus Genomics is a Series A-stage biotech company that has raised $32M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 3 public comparables in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of three valuation methods examined, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses total capital raised ($32M) as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $64M. Peer-Median comparison was not feasible due to insufficient granular peer data—while 7 same-sector peers exist, none met the filtering criteria of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier valuation (minimum 3 required). Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied because Nucleus Genomics' revenue is not on file, and private companies rarely disclose such metrics; the public sector median P/S of 9.2x therefore cannot be operationalized.

Given the single applicable method, the analysis supports a valuation range of $54M (low) to $74M (high), centered on $64M. The primary uncertainty is lack of financial detail on the target, which precludes revenue-based and peer-relative approaches. Any refinement would require disclosure of revenue, customer traction, or confirmed financial metrics that would enable peer-median or public-comp triangulation.
